findings.title: Night route as a disclosure corridor
findings.claim: The focus's night journey from a protected departure place toward a far destination is explicitly aimed at showing signs. Wider passages repeat night movement with servants, travel through blessed settlements, protected sanctuary language, and the showing of signs, so the route can be heard as a directed corridor of disclosure.
findings.mechanism: The carrier أَسْرَىٰ at 17:1:3:1 takes on its night-travel branch as لَيْلًا and the مِن ... إِلَى route give it independent temporal and spatial structure. The focus's purpose clause لِنُرِيَهُ مِنْ آيَاتِنَا meets the exact showing-of-signs wording in 20:23; 44:23 repeats night movement with servants, 22:25 gives the Sacred Mosque a protected shared-space frame, and 34:18 joins night/day travel to blessed settlements and safety. The legacy-described 17:2-6 transfer sequence adds a channel-like image, while 21:71 supplies another movement toward a blessed land.
findings.reader_payoff: Movement, destination, and perception become one directed act: the journey carries the reader toward a showing, while its night, protected origin, and blessed destination remain perceptible together.
findings.containment: The scenes in 20:23, 21:71, 22:25, 34:18, and 44:23 are distinct and do not identify the same sites or event. The 17:2-6 and 17:12 descriptions remain source-attributed; 17:78 has exact Arabic in the packet. root_000702/B002 contributes only a small-stream analogy: the focus verb remains night travel, with no literal water route claimed.

epistemic.reason: The trusted cross-run record anchors its core branches to exact focus words. Wider parallels include direct target Arabic as well as legacy reader descriptions, and the channel facet is analogical.

findings.title: Showing and public response
findings.claim: The focus states that the journey is to show signs to the servant; the later 17:60 names a vision shown to the addressee as a trial for people. This supplies a bounded audience-response dimension to the focus's disclosure.
findings.mechanism: The carrier لِنُرِيَهُ at 17:1:15:2 makes seeing the purpose of movement. The exact 17:60 Arabic describes a vision shown to the addressee as a fitna for people. Their contact changes showing from private perception alone into disclosure whose reception can test an audience.
findings.reader_payoff: The signs' significance can extend beyond what the traveler sees to how people respond to a shown vision.
findings.containment: 17:60 may refer to a distinct vision and trial; the packet does not equate it with the event in 17:1 or settle the vision's referent. The connection is retained from supplied Arabic, without inventing target morphology.

epistemic.reason: The focus purpose and 17:60 surface are both supplied, but the connection is a missing-ayah suggestion and its label is not an acceptance decision.
